name: Trinity College Dublin
description: Trinity College Dublin, the University of Dublin, is Ireland's oldest university, founded by royal charter in 1592 in central Dublin. It has about 22,000 students across arts, humanities, business, law, engineering, science and health sciences.
whyIncluded: Its MB BCh BAO is on the Singapore Medical Council's list of registrable basic medical qualifications, and Trinity has awarded physiotherapy and occupational therapy degrees in Singapore with the Singapore Institute of Technology since 2012.

livingCosts.summary: Trinity's own estimate for international undergraduates: housing, bills, food, transport and personal costs, spread over 9 months. Excludes immigration fees, health insurance and flights.
livingCosts.notes: Trinity's 'Cost of Living' page for international students (updated 16 July 2026) gives annual ranges; each is taken at its midpoint and divided by 9 months. Housing = average of Trinity Hall (EUR 7,227, Sept-June) and Kavanagh Court (EUR 12,350) undergraduate accommodation plus utilities EUR 1,000-2,000; food = meals EUR 3,000-5,000; transport = commuting EUR 1,000; personal = miscellaneous EUR 2,500 (personal items, leisure, course materials) plus personal and social EUR 2,000-3,000. Excludes immigration fees, health insurance and airfares. Trinity's own total undergraduate estimate is EUR 19,937-29,050 a year.

programmes.name: Computer Science (BA, integrated MAI)
programmes.summary: First-year tuition for international (non-EU) students plus about EUR 213 in student levies. Fees rise 2.33% a year for later years, so the total will be higher. A fifth master's year is charged at the higher postgraduate rate.
programmes.notes: Non-EU tuition for new entrants in 2026/27 (course code UICS-ICSC-2F); the schedule says the fee is for the first year only. Compulsory fee is the Student Levies and Charges (SLC) for a full-time 4-year degree (EUR 212.75 in 2026/27, of which EUR 8 AMLE membership is optional). Year 5 of the integrated master's is charged at the postgraduate rate. Trinity's Fee Certainty policy sets the annual increase for the 2026/27 intake at 2.33% a year for 2027/28-2030/31, so fees are not fixed for the programme.
